To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

copper (I) oxide shows NTE at low temperatures due to geometric distortions of tetrahedral units and silver (I), on the contrary, shows NTE at high temperatures, due to a change in coordination number of the metal cations.
the NTE in Cu 2 O is due to geometric distortions of tetrahedral units and that the NTE of Ag 2 O is related to local structural distortions.

1) the negative thermal expansion observed in Cu 2 O and Ag 2 O is due to a change in their structure at high temperature, and not due to a change of the unit cell parameters; and 2) the structural change is related to a local distortion of the tetrahedra, which is not observed in Cu 1−x Ag x O.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the negative thermal contraction and expansion of cuprite structures.
the study of NTE in cuprite structures by means of the PDF analysis.
the understanding of the NTE in Cu 2 O and Ag 2 O by means of a temperature-dependent PDF analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the negative thermal expansion observed in these compounds is not related to a change of the tetrahedra solid angle.

the NTE of Cu 2 O is related to a change from tetrahedral to trigonal symmetry of the polyhedron at about 200–250 K, and the NTE of Ag 2 O to the presence of local tetrahedral distortions at all temperatures.
Cu 2 O is more prone to distortions than Ag 2 O, and this is related to its higher thermal expansion coefficient, which is about twice the value of silver oxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NTE is related to a structural distortion that involves the tetrahedral unit.
the NTE of cuprite-type compounds is due to a change in solid angle of the tetrahedra, which is related to the change of the bond angle of the O-Cu-O units.

the NTE in Cu 2 O is related to a change of the solid angle of CuO 4 tetrahedra, while Ag 3 O 4 is a rigid structure that shows a NTE due to anharmonic motions of the Ag atoms, which are probably related to the presence of a large thermal motion of Ag atoms at low temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NTE in these two compounds is not due to the same mechanism, and that PDF analysis is an effective tool to study local structural changes.
the negative thermal expansion observed in cuprite-type structures is not a simple consequence of the thermal vibrations of the atoms.
the NTE of cuprite-type compounds is not related to the presence of a local structural transition.
